insight.title: Spiral Staircases Are Designed for Single File
insight.subtitle: The extreme geometry of spiral stairs prioritizes space efficiency over smooth, shared movement.
insight.notificationHook: Spiral stairs: one person at a time

sections.text: Ever notice how spiral staircases always have a tiny, awkward inner edge? It feels like you're constantly fighting for balance, making two-way traffic or carrying anything a clumsy dance.

This isn't an oversight. Spiral stairs are a triumph of compact design, maximizing vertical travel in minimal floor space. That razor-thin inner curve is the geometric necessity of their tight, rotational form.

By forcing you to walk more cautiously and single-file, the design subtly manages flow and inherent safety risks. It's a space-saving solution that implicitly dictates how, and how many, people can pass.
